key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over hours to days. LOCATION: BILATERAL kidney involvement. DURATION: Develops over hours to days, may persist for days to weeks. CHARACTER: DECREASED urine output, swelling, fluid retention. AGGRAVATING: DEHYDRATION, medications, contrast agents. RELIEVING: FLUID management, dialysis if severe. TIMING: Gradual onset, develops over hours to days. SEVERITY: 6-9/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: DECREASED URINE OUTPUT, swelling, fluid retention, may have nausea, vomiting, confusion, may have electrolyte imbalances. KEY POSITIVES: Decreased urine output, swelling, fluid retention, elevated creatinine, elevated BUN. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe fluid overload with respiratory distress - possible pulmonary edema, call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of uremia - confusion, seizures, coma - call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
